title: Check: RBAC
description: Five questions on who may do what.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a Role and a ClusterRole?

options.text: A Role is for users, a ClusterRole for ServiceAccounts
A Role is namespaced; a ClusterRole is cluster-scoped and can also cover non-namespaced resources

questions.explanation: A ClusterRole can also be reused inside one namespace by referencing it from a RoleBinding.

questions.prompt: A RoleBinding in namespace `dev` references a ClusterRole. What is granted?

options.text: Those permissions, but only within dev

questions.explanation: Which is the standard way to reuse a role like `view` per namespace without redefining it.

questions.prompt: RBAC has no deny rules. What follows?

options.text: Permissions are purely additive - the union of everything that matches

questions.explanation: You cannot subtract a permission; you grant less instead.

questions.prompt: Write the command that checks whether you may create Deployments in namespace dev.
accepted_answers: kubectl auth can-i create deployments -n dev
kubectl auth can-i create deployment -n dev
kubectl auth can-i create deployments --namespace dev
questions.explanation: Add `--as=system:serviceaccount:dev:build` to ask the same question as somebody else.

questions.prompt: Which subject kinds may a binding reference?
questions.explanation: Users and groups come from the authentication layer; Kubernetes stores no user objects of its own.
